title.value: Tau-targeting antisense oligonucleotide MAPT Rx in mild Alzheimer’s disease: a phase 1b, randomized, placebo-controlled trial
title.quote: Tau-targeting antisense oligonucleotide MAPT Rx in mild Alzheimer’s disease: a phase 1b, randomized, placebo-controlled trial

design.value: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multiple-ascending dose phase 1b trial
design.quote: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multiple-ascending dose phase 1b trial evaluated the safety, pharmacokinetics and target engagement of MAPT Rx .

n.quote: Forty-six patients enrolled in the trial

population.value: mild AD, defined by a CDR Overall Global Score of 1 or Global Score of 0.5 with a Memory Score of 1, Mini-Mental State Examination score (MMSE ) of 20–27 inclusive
population.quote: Eligible participants were between the ages of 50 and 74 years and had mild AD, defined by a CDR Overall Global Score of 1 or Global Score of 0.5 with a Memory Score of 1, Mini-Mental State Examination score (MMSE ) of 20–27 inclusive

biomarker_confirmation.value: CSF pattern of low Aβ42 and elevated t-tau and p-tau consistent with diagnosis of AD
biomarker_confirmation.quote: CSF pattern of low Aβ42 and elevated t-tau and p-tau consistent with diagnosis of AD

comparator.quote: Four ascending dose cohorts were enrolled sequentially and randomized 3:1 to intrathecal bolus administrations of MAPT Rx or placebo

followup.value: 13-week treatment period, followed by a 23 week post-treatment period
followup.quote: 13-week treatment period, followed by a 23 week post-treatment period

intervention.value: intrathecal bolus administrations of MAPT Rx or placebo every 4 or 12 weeks
intervention.quote: intrathecal bolus administrations of MAPT Rx or placebo every 4 or 12 weeks

n_description.quote: Forty-six patients enrolled in the trial

phase.quote: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multiple-ascending dose phase 1b trial

outcomes.name: MAPT Rx pharmacokinetics in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)
outcomes.quote: The secondary endpoint was MAPT Rx pharmacokinetics in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

outcomes.name: CSF total-tau protein concentration
outcomes.quote: The prespecified key exploratory outcome was CSF total-tau protein concentration.
outcomes.prespecification_evidence: The prespecified key exploratory outcome was CSF total-tau protein concentration.

primary_endpoint_status.quote: Overall MAPT Rx treatment was generally well tolerated, with all participants completing the treatment period and over 90% of participants completing the post-treatment period.
primary_endpoint_status.explanation: The trial evaluated safety as its primary endpoint and found the drug to be well tolerated with no severe or serious adverse events in the treatment groups.

harms.name: death
harms.quote: There were no deaths, dose-limiting AEs or discontinuations of dosing regimens during the trial.

deaths.quote: There were no deaths, dose-limiting AEs or discontinuations of dosing regimens during the trial.

discontinuations.quote: Three participants (6.5%) voluntarily withdrew from the study during the post-treatment period

serious_adverse_events.quote: Two serious AEs occurred in two participants receiving placebo: hospitalization due to diverticulitis and an emergency room visit due to a minor stroke from which both participants recovered.

limitations: This first-in-human study of MAPT Rx has several limitations mainly due to its small size ( N = 46) as is typical of phase 1 studies.
interpretation of the clinical meaningfulness of these results is limited due to the combination of assay variability and small sample size.

this study was conducted in relatively young participants with mild AD, and it will be important that future studies of MAPT Rx evaluate safety and efficacy in an older population, which may be more representative of late-onset AD.
